notes: w1 carries ink along the crop edge, but the tops of the figures are cut off by that edge: a figure-eight-like glyph followed by three slanted loops, and further along a bowl-and-stem glyph with a full stop. w2-w5 are blank paper, a tear and perforations. Not readable as a date.

w1, at the crop edge, which cuts the tops of the figures. Roll number 930 and 23. 6. are firm; the month could be an 8 with its open upper loop cut away, and the final group is two slanted strokes that read as 11 but could be 17. w2-w5 blank paper and perforations.

w1 carries one long cursive word written across the roll rather than along it, with a wide closing flourish; it looks like a signature, not a workshop date. w2-w4 show a taped hole, stains and perforations only.

Printed leader label with the catalogue entry and a printed care notice (rolls to be kept in boxes, basin of water, etc.), partly torn away at the left. 245 is the printed catalogue number, not a written roll number. No punch date; w2 and w3 show stained paper and perforations only.

inscription: [t]he end of the roll / dated / 31. III. 1909 / (18.12.1989) / 90 years on
notes: A later English hand, dated by itself 18.12.1989, written across the roll near the torn end. It reports that the end of the roll is dated 31 March 1909, but that workshop inscription is not itself in any of these crops, so the 1909 date here is second hand. w1 has a small scribbled mark at the crop edge, cut off and illegible; w2 and w3 show the roll edge and perforations.

Pencil along the crop edge in w1; the wider crop brings in the roll number 415 that the first crop cut away. The 8 is a plain double loop, not the open-topped form. The initials after the date read Mb., though only the M is certain. w2-w4 show perforations, a taped hole and a damp stain.

inscription: WELTE-MIGNON No. 422 / Impromptu / G major, Op. 90, No. 3 / Fr. Schubert / Played by [signature] -- and a later English hand ending "29. 8. 1984"
notes: w5 is the leader: the printed catalogue label for Welte-Mignon 422 and a long pencil note in English by a later owner, signed off 29.8.1984, commenting on a flaw in the treble cut and comparing the roll with Carreno. Not a workshop date. w1 does carry a short pencil line at the crop edge, but only the feet of the figures survive the cut and it cannot be read. w2-w4 are paper, stains and perforations.

inscription: 26303   [w2:] 469   [w4 label:] WELTE-MIGNON No. 466  Hexentanz  Op. 17 No. 2  MacDowell  Played by [signature]
notes: w1 carries five figures in heavy ink at the crop edge, tops cut: 2 6 3 0 3. Taken as an unseparated date in the workshop manner this would be 26.3.03, but that is a year earlier than anything else read in this corpus and the fourth figure could as well be an 8 with its upper loop cut away, so I would not enter it as a date; it may equally be a production or serial number. w2 carries a separate three-figure number 469, also at the edge, which disagrees with the 466 on the printed leader label in w4.

Pencil across the roll near the edge in w2, on a coarsely textured stretch, so the strokes are broken but the figures are all there: a four-figure number, a dash, then 26. 1. 26. The written number 4191 disagrees with the printed leader label in w3, which reads No. 568. Valse Op. 70. Chopin, with the facsimile signature Lamond and the printed recording date 27. IX. 05 -- that printed 1905 date is the recording, not the punching of this copy.

The wider crop does not free the line from the edge -- the tops of the figures are still shaved off -- but it does show the whole of it, and enough to settle the two doubts. The month figure carries a long tail well below the baseline, which an 8 in this hand does not, so it is a 9. The second figure of the year is a broad rounded bowl open at the upper left; the 5 of the roll number 5700, a few centimetres away in the same hand, is a narrow hook with a small lower bowl, and an 8 would close on the left, so I read 3. Reading 4 September 1913. The number 5700 is higher than the T-100 catalogue runs, so it may be a job number rather than a catalogue number. No initials follow.

The wider re-render does not help on this roll: w1 and w2 put the writing hard against the crop edge and shear the tops off the figures, while the original crops 1 and 2 hold the same two lines whole, so that is where I read them. Crop 1, pencil, one line: 2 7 . 4 . 1 7 . Both sevens carry the German crossbar and match each other, which settles 27 against 24 and 17 against 14; the month is the open German 4; each group closes with a point. 27 April 1917. Crop 2, in the same pencil and the same hand, carries four figures 2948 with a closing point, which I take for the roll number. Crop 3 and w3 are blank paper with perforations. Crop w4 is the leader, carrying a long pencil note in English by a later owner about the bass and treble cut and the end of the roll; it is not a workshop inscription and gives no date. Second reader, from w1 only: the same line is legible there in spite of the shaved tops, because both sevens keep their German crossbars and the month figure keeps the open 4 -- 27. 4. 17. confirmed independently.

inscription: [w3 label:] WELTE-MIGNON No. 1263  Minuett  G major  Paderewsky  Played by [signature]
notes: Two short lines of ink sit on the crop edge, one in w1 and one in w2, each four figures long; both are cut through the middle and I can only say that the w2 one looks like 4965 and the w1 one like 4194 or 1194. Neither is separated as a date. The printed leader label in w3 gives the catalogue number 1263 for the Paderewski Minuet. w4 is stained paper.

The wider crop lifts the whole line clear of the edge for once, so nothing is cut. Ink, one line, in the same layout as the known 225. Fritz. 18 Jan 09.: number, puncher, then the date with the month written out. 20 Nov 1908, all four figures of the year plain. The third figure of the roll number is the one soft spot -- 1226 or 1236 -- the rest of the line is firm. w2-w4 show perforations and stained paper.

w1 has two short groups of figures lying along the crop edge, and the edge takes the upper two thirds of every figure. The first group is four figures and would fit 1480, which is the catalogue number on the printed leader label in w3 (Peer Gynt II), but I cannot vouch for it; the second group, where a date would stand, leaves only feet. w2 and w4 are torn and perforated paper.

inscription: WELTE-MIGNON No. 2159  Concert  E-moll, Op. 11, I. Teil  Fr. Chopin  Gespielt von [signature]
notes: Only the printed German leader label, with a facsimile signature under Gespielt von and no date. w1-w3 are plain and perforated paper with two small repairs; the wider crops bring in no writing at all, so this roll simply has no workshop inscription in the places that were cropped.

w1 carries four ink figures clear of the edge and whole: 8 6 2 2. The first has both loops, the second a single bowl under a long curve, so they are 8 and 6 and not two of the same figure. Read in the workshop way with the points dropped this is 8. 6. 22. The doubt is whether it is a date at all: w4 carries a second four-figure group, 4588, in the same ink and the same place on the paper, and that one cannot be a date, so the pair may both be numbers. w3 holds a later English hand, Finish of Funeral March, with a ruled line across the roll marking the spot; that is a listener/owner note, not a workshop date. w2 and w5 are blank and stained.

inscription: 592 (region w4)  |  a line of five or six figures in region w2, opening 9 1, not resolved
notes: w4 carries 592 in ink, which agrees with the printed leader label (Welte-Mignon No. 592, Waltzes Op. 39 Nos. 15 and 16, Brahms, played by G. Galston, on w5). w2 carries the only other inscription, a single line of figures cut along the top by the crop edge exactly as in the original crop 2, so the wider render gains nothing. The line falls into two groups with one clear gap: first two figures that read 9 and 1, the 9 a closed loop with a long tail below the line; then, after the gap, four more, the first an oval under an open upper loop which is either 8 or 6, then two narrow figures and a closing diagonal with a crossbar. Read straight through, 91824 or 91624, it does not fall into a day, a month and a two-figure year in the German order, and with the tops of the figures gone I cannot say which figure I have wrong. I have therefore left the date empty rather than force it. w1 and w3 are blank paper with a crease, w6 the scanner's QPcard colour target. Second reader: agreed. In w2 the crop edge takes everything above the feet of the figures, and no amount of flattening the paper texture brings the heads back. Two groups, six figures, and no grouping of them falls into a German day, month and year. Nothing to enter.

A stamp, not a hand, set across the roll in w1 and well clear of the crop edge. Five marks and a point: a heavy leading mark shaped like a serif 1 but carrying a smear of ink at its foot, then 9, 8, an over-inked figure with a counter above a solid base which I take for 2, and 5. Read straight through this is 19. 8. 25. The warning about the stamped rolls applies here: the figures without the leading mark, 9825, already make a possible date, 9. 8. 25., so the day is either 9 or 19 and I cannot choose between them from this impression alone. August 1925 is firm; the fourth figure would have to be a 0 for 1905, and it is not an even ring. w2-w4 show a torn edge, tissue and perforations, with no second impression of the same stamp to compare the leading mark against.

inscription: 291122   [w4 label:] WELTE-MIGNON No. 2822  Thais  Fantasia mosaic  J. Massenet  Played by P. Gayraud
notes: Six ink figures run along the crop edge in w1 with no separators, in the manner of the 311022 already read in this corpus: 2 9, then two plain upright strokes, then 2 2. The tops are shaved by the edge, but the second figure keeps a tail that drops well below the line and curls left, which makes it a 9 and not a 3, and the month pair shows two straight strokes with no bowl, so 11 and not 10. 29 November 1922. The printed leader label in w4 gives the catalogue number 2822 for the Thais fantasia played by Gayraud; the roll itself carries no written number in these crops.

Pale buff paper with fine laid lines, the writing a thin pencil, and the line is whole in both the wider crop w1 and the original crop 1 (the same line shows again, cut off at the crop edge, at the right of w3). It runs number, date, name in the usual order: first a group of five figures whose last four read 1953 and whose first is a tall looped stroke that could be an 8 or a number sign, then 24 Nov in a clear hand, the 2 and 4 plain and the month in Latin letters as in the 18 Jan 09 pattern, then a cursive word of five or six letters ending in a long ascender, which looks like a name of the Siegel or Segal kind but which I will not put down as read. There is no year with the day and month, so I have left date_iso empty: 24 November of an unstated year. If the figures before it are the roll number rather than a year written out, then 1953 is that number. w4, w5 and w7 are blank paper, w6 the printed licence notice, w8 the leader tab and spool. Second reader, from w1 and w3: I first took the group after the day for four figures, 1108, which would have given November 1908, and that is wrong. Set beside the 20 Nov 1908 on mh255vw4599, written by this same workshop with the month in Latin letters, the group matches Nov stroke for stroke: the tall stroke and arch of the N, the o, the v. So there is no year in it. Nothing at all follows the closing word to the right, so the line carries no year anywhere: 24 November, year unstated. On the opening figures I read a leading looped mark and then four, of which the second drops a tail below the line, so 1953 rather than 1253; either way it is four figures and cannot be read as the catalogue 194, so that disagreement stands.

A stamp set along the roll in w1 and, unusually for this batch, well clear of the crop edge. Column measurement gives five figures and then a separate low broken mark: 2 4 0 2 4, mark. The identical stamp on tb323rh4122 reads 9 1 0 2 4 and is followed by the same mark in the same place, which confirms that the mark belongs to the slug and that five figures is the whole date. Five figures here leave no possible month: 24, 0, 24. The day 24 and the year 24 are plain, the middle figure prints as a clean oval and must be an understruck month, so I enter the year only. w2-w5 show a tear, perforations and blank leader.

A stamp along the roll in w1, clear of the crop edge and cleanly struck: 9 1 0 2 4, read in the upper panel as it stands. Five figures with the points dropped give 9. 10. 24., 9 October 1924. A low broken mark follows the figures; the same mark follows the stamp on gy310qs3678 in this same batch, which suggests it belongs to the slug rather than to the date. Nothing stands before the 9, so the day here is not in the doubt that the warning about the leading blob describes. w2-w4 show plain paper, perforations and a splice.

inscription: WELTE-MIGNON No. 3045  Preludes  1) La fille aux cheveux de lin  2) La Puerta del vino  Cl. Debussy  Played by [signature]
notes: Only the printed leader label, with no date on it. w1-w3 are plain paper with a tar-like stain and a few perforations; the wider crops add nothing written. Nothing on this roll to date it by.

A faint hard pencil on pale paper, one line in w1 and in the original crop 1, which holds it whole; the wider crop shears the tops of the figures against its edge, so I read from crop 1. Two groups: first four figures 2685, then the date in three, 16, 8 and 27, each closed with a point. The first group agrees with the printed leader label on w2, which reads WELTE-MIGNON. 2685 / NEARER MY GOD TO THEE. / MASON. / Played by E. ADAM., and I had read the figures before I saw the label. In the date group the closing 7 carries the German crossbar, the 6 is a plain bowl and the 8 a loop over a bowl rather than the open-topped form, so 16 August 1927. I have kept this at medium rather than high only because the pencil is so light that single strokes drop out in places. w3 is blank paper and w4 shows perforations only. Second reader, from w1 alone: the cut leaves 16, then one bowl, then two strokes, which is what 16 8 27 looks like with the heads of the 8, the 2 and the 7 shorn off. Nothing in the wider crop contradicts the reading from crop 1, and nothing in it would have settled the figures either.
